rationale: The two on-record all-PASS designs are 110cm polyethylene+5cm lead (mass 1.6e3 kg/m2, R3 photon [1.02,1.1] vs 3 limit) and 105cm polyethylene+5cm lead (mass 1.55e3 kg/m2, R3 [1.17,1.28]). Both have R3 margin of roughly 2.3-2.7x below the 3 uSv/h limit, while lead costs ~113.5 kg/m2/cm versus polyethylene's ~9.4 kg/m2/cm, so lead thickness is the highest-leverage mass lever. This design trims lead from 5 to 4cm while raising polyethylene from 105 to 108cm (between the two known-good poly thicknesses) to protect the R2 neutron margin, which on record tightens fast with less moderator (105cm+5cm lead R2 upper=6.63 vs 110cm+5cm lead R2 upper=3.44).

More aggressive sibling of the 108+4 candidate: same 4cm lead cut from the 105/110+5cm all-PASS baselines, but only 1cm of extra polyethylene over the 105cm baseline instead of 3cm, to see how much R2 margin above the 105cm+5cm lead result (R2 upper 6.63 of 7) is actually needed once lead is thinner. Tests the boundary between this and the 108+4 candidate.

Uses the more generous R2 margin from the 110cm polyethylene point (bare and with 5cm lead both show comfortable neutron passes, e.g. 110cm+5cm lead R2 upper=3.44 of 7, over 2x margin) to absorb a larger, 2cm lead cut. Comparing 5cm-lead vs 10cm-lead photon results at matched polyethylene thickness (e.g. 90cm poly+10cm lead R3 mid~0.21 vs the much higher photon at 90cm poly+5cm lead extrapolated from the 96/100/105/110+5cm lead trend) implies roughly a 2-3x reduction in photon dose per added cm of lead in this regime, so cutting 2cm from the 5cm baseline is a meaningful but plausibly still-passing step given the 110+5cm baseline's photon dose (1.02-1.1) started well under the 3 limit.

Bare 105cm borated_polyethylene (no lead) is already on record: R2=[4.44,5.96] pass (15% margin below 7) and R3=[8.35,8.84] fail. Bare 110cm borated_polyethylene R3=[6.98,7.39] is roughly half of bare 110cm polyethylene's R3=[15.6,15.9], showing boron's low-yield capture (displacing hydrogen's 2.2 MeV capture gamma) sharply cuts photon production per unit thickness versus plain polyethylene, even though both pass R2 similarly at 110cm (borated [2.49,4.88] vs plain [2.71,4.4]). Since the borated column already starts photon production roughly 2x lower than plain poly, it should need much less lead than the 5cm plain-poly baseline to clear the 3 uSv/h R3 limit. This is an unexplored region of the constellation: no borated_polyethylene+lead combination has been transported yet.

Boundary probe paired with the 105cm borated_polyethylene+3cm lead candidate: same moderator column, 1cm less lead, to bracket the minimum lead thickness the borated column needs against R3. If bare 105cm borated_polyethylene R3 upper (8.84) needs roughly a 3x reduction to clear 3 uSv/h and each cm of lead is worth roughly 2-3x (per the 5cm-vs-10cm-lead photon comparison at matched polyethylene thickness elsewhere in the constellation), 2cm may fall short while 3cm clears it; running both pins the boundary in one round. Mass would be only ~1.28e3 kg/m2 if it passes, well below any all-PASS design on record.

Hedge on the 105cm borated_polyethylene+3cm lead candidate: same lead thickness, but using the 110cm borated_polyethylene point instead, which on record has more R2 margin bare (R2=[2.49,4.88], upper 4.88 of 7) than the 105cm point (upper 5.96 of 7) and a lower bare R3 (6.98-7.39 vs 8.35-8.84). If the 105+3 candidate's R2 margin turns out to be too thin once the moderator is borated (an untested combination), this design should still pass both R2 and R3 with more room, at the cost of ~5cm more moderator (~50 kg/m2).

Second boundary probe, pairing with the 105+2cm candidate at the higher, safer 110cm borated_polyethylene moderator thickness. Bare 110cm borated_polyethylene has more R2 margin (upper 4.88 of 7) and lower bare R3 (upper 7.39) than the 105cm point, so if 105+2cm fails on R3, this indicates whether 2cm lead is close to sufficient once the moderator column itself is more generous, separating an R3 shortfall from an R2 shortfall.

Hybrid testing whether most of boron's photon benefit can be captured with a thin borated_polyethylene layer placed just ahead of the lead cap rather than borating the whole column. Capture gammas produced deep in the front of a thick moderator are already largely self-absorbed by the time they would reach the exit face; the ones that matter for R3 are those produced near the back, close to the lead. Using cheaper plain polyethylene (9.4 kg/m2/cm) for the bulk of the column and reserving borated_polyethylene (10.0 kg/m2/cm) for the last 10cm before the lead tests whether the lighter hybrid still gets close to the full-borated-column photon suppression seen in the 105/110cm bare borated_polyethylene records.

Variant of the plain/borated hybrid with more total moderator (108cm vs 105cm) and a slightly thinner borated interlayer, to see how R2 and R3 trade off against the 95+10+3 hybrid candidate once real transport data is available for that geometry.

Cleanest single-variable comparison to the exact on-record all-PASS design 105cm polyethylene+5cm lead: holds polyethylene fixed at 105cm and cuts only lead, from 5 to 4cm, isolating lead's marginal effect on R2 and R3 from any change in moderator thickness. Directly tests whether the 105+5cm baseline's R3 margin (upper 1.28 of 3, over 2x headroom) survives a 1cm lead cut on its own before combining it with any polyethylene increase.

Testing the unexplored borated_polyethylene+lead region. Bare 105cm borated_polyethylene is already on record passing R2 (upper 5.96 of 7) and failing only R3 (8.35-8.84 of 3 limit). Bare borated_polyethylene shows roughly half the photon output of plain polyethylene at matched thickness (110cm borated R3 6.98-7.39 vs 110cm plain R3 15.6-15.9), consistent with boron's low-yield capture displacing hydrogen's 2.2 MeV capture gamma. l-0003 (105+3cm lead) is the primary bet that a much thinner lead cap than the 5cm used in the two on-record all-PASS designs suffices once the moderator itself suppresses gamma production; l-0004 (105+2cm lead) is the aggressive probe on the same moderator column to bracket the minimum lead needed; l-0005 (110+3cm lead) hedges with more R2 margin in case the borated column's neutron performance under lead differs from the plain-poly analogy.

105cm borated_polyethylene + 2cm lead (l-0004) just transported all-PASS at 1.28e3 kg/m2, but R3 margin was razor-thin (upper 2.98 of 3, margin 0.0239 uSv/h). Since borated_polyethylene (10.0 kg/m2/cm) costs slightly more than plain polyethylene (9.4 kg/m2/cm), and boron's mechanism is local capture-gamma suppression, this candidate keeps the same 105cm total moderator thickness and 2cm lead but pushes most of the column back to cheaper plain polyethylene, keeping only the last 15cm (nearest the lead) borated, to test how much of l-0004's R3 performance survives with far less borated material and correspondingly lower mass (1.22e3 kg/m2 if it holds).

Same design as the 90+15+2 hybrid (matching l-0004's 105cm total moderator + 2cm lead, at the boundary already established there) but with more borated coverage (35cm instead of 15cm) to hedge against the possibility that capture-gamma production is not concentrated right at the back of the slab, in case a thin 15cm borated zone under-covers the region that matters for R3.

Third point on the same plain/borated split sweep at fixed 105cm total moderator + 2cm lead (matching l-0004's boundary case), with roughly half the column borated, to help locate where along the split R3 crosses back over the 3 uSv/h limit.

Fourth point on the plain/borated split sweep at fixed 105cm total moderator + 2cm lead: mostly borated with only 30cm plain polyethylene at the front. Completes a sweep (15, 35, 55, 75cm borated, all with 105cm total and 2cm lead) bracketing between the full 105cm all-borated case that already passed razor-thin (l-0004) and the all-plain case that is known to fail R3 badly without adequate lead (e.g. 110cm plain polyethylene alone R3 15.6-15.9).

l-0004 (105cm borated_polyethylene + 2cm lead) passed all-PASS but with R3 upper bound 2.98 against the 3 limit, essentially at the noise floor. This candidate adds 2cm more borated_polyethylene (mass cost only ~19 kg/m2) to check whether a small increase gives meaningfully more R3 margin, as a less knife-edge alternative near the same mass class (1.3e3 kg/m2).

Boundary probe just below l-0004 (105cm borated_polyethylene + 2cm lead, R3 upper 2.98 of 3): 1cm less borated_polyethylene, to see whether the true R3 boundary at 2cm lead sits at 105cm or whether 104cm (mass 1.27e3 kg/m2, lighter still) also clears it. Given R3 rose from 1.76 (3cm lead, l-0003) to 2.98 (2cm lead, l-0004) as lead alone dropped 1cm, R3 is clearly sensitive at this boundary, so this checks whether it is equally sensitive to 1cm of moderator.

Three-way test after l-0004 (105cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead) passed all-PASS at 1.28e3 kg/m2 but with R3 razor-thin (upper 2.98 of 3 limit). l-0010 (90cm polyethylene+15cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, mass 1.22e3) and l-0012 (50cm polyethylene+55cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, mass 1.25e3) hold the same 105cm total moderator and 2cm lead as l-0004 but swap varying amounts of the front of the column from borated to cheaper plain polyethylene, testing whether boron's local capture-gamma suppression is only needed near the back of the slab (since little thermal capture happens in the still-epithermal front region regardless of composition) or is needed throughout; either result is informative and either could beat l-0004 on mass. l-0006 (110cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, screened in round 1, mass 1.33e3) is a hedge: bare 110cm borated_polyethylene has more R2 and R3 margin than bare 105cm (R2 upper 4.88 vs 5.96, R3 upper 7.39 vs 8.84), so it should give a materially healthier R3 margin than l-0004's near-zero one while still beating every prior all-PASS design's mass by over 200 kg/m2, regardless of whether the hybrid hypothesis pans out.

Round 3, following up on round 2: the hybrid plain/borated split (l-0010: 15cm borated backing, l-0012: 55cm borated backing) failed R3 at both points (5.37-5.66 and 4.73-4.92 respectively, both over the 3 limit), showing capture-gamma suppression needs most of the column borated, not just a back layer -- so the hybrid direction is abandoned; any hybrid light enough to matter would need to be almost entirely borated anyway, saving only a few kg/m2 versus the all-borated column. l-0006 (110cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead) passed all-PASS with healthy margins (R2 upper 3.78 of 7, R3 upper 2.52 of 3), unlike l-0004 (105cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, all-PASS but R3 upper 2.98 of 3, essentially at the noise floor). This round tests the pure-borated+2cm-lead family at three more points, all already screened in round 2: l-0015 (104cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, mass 1.27e3 kg/m2) checks whether 105cm is truly the minimum moderator thickness at 2cm lead or whether 104cm also clears R3, since l-0004 was already right at the edge; l-0014 (107cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, mass 1.3e3 kg/m2) checks for a middle option with healthier R3 margin than l-0004 but less mass than l-0006; l-0013 (30cm polyethylene+75cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead, mass 1.26e3 kg/m2) is a last, low-cost check on the hybrid trend (R3 improved from 5.5 at 15cm borated to 4.8 at 55cm borated) in case the trend accelerates enough by 75cm borated to clear 3, which would be a small additional mass win over l-0004.

Fills the one-cm gap in the now-tightly-bracketed R3 boundary at 2cm lead: 104cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead (l-0015) came back R3 inconclusive (upper 3.07 of 3, essentially straddling the limit), 105cm (l-0004) passed with R3 upper 2.98 of 3 (margin 0.0239, effectively at the noise floor), and 107cm (l-0014) passed with a moderate margin (R3 upper 2.78, margin 0.218). This will not beat l-0004 on mass (1.29e3 kg/m2 vs 1.277e3 kg/m2) but pins down whether the R3 margin grows smoothly from 105 to 107, which matters for judging how much confidence to place in 105cm as the practical floor versus recommending a slightly heavier design with real margin.

Fills the 1cm gap between 105cm borated_polyethylene+2cm lead (l-0004, all-PASS, R3 upper 2.98 of 3, margin 0.0239, current lightest record at 1.277e3 kg/m2) and 107cm (l-0014, all-PASS, R3 upper 2.78, margin 0.218), to characterize how quickly R3 margin recovers moving away from the 104cm inconclusive boundary (l-0015, R3 upper 3.07). Not expected to beat l-0004 on mass; this is for confidence in recommending 105cm as the practical floor versus a design with real margin.
